"Create a brand-new programming language called E# (E-Sharp).

E# should be a real programming language designed to look and feel like simple English. The goal is to make programming understandable to beginners while still being powerful enough to create games, applications, tools, and interactive projects.

TAGLINE:
\"Code in English.\"

==================================================
1. VARIABLE SYSTEM
==================================================

The main variable syntax must be:

Let [name] be [value]

Examples:

Let name be \"Player\"
Let score be 0
Let speed be 5
Let gravity be 9.8
Let isAlive be true
Let message be \"Hello world\"
Let nothing be null

The value can be different data types, including:

- Text/string
- Whole numbers
- Decimal numbers
- True/false values
- Null
- Lists
- Objects
- Expressions
- Other variables

Examples:

Let score be 10 + 5
Let total be score * 2
Let playerName be name

E# should automatically determine the type of the value.

To change an existing variable, use:

Set score to 100
Set name to \"New Player\"
Set isAlive to false

Do NOT require traditional syntax such as:

score = 100
let score = 100;
var score = 100;

E# should use natural English syntax instead.

==================================================
2. OUTPUT
==================================================

Use:

Say \"Hello world\"

Variables can be included:

Say name
Say \"Hello \" + name
Say \"Score: \" + score

==================================================
3. CONDITIONS
==================================================

Use English-like conditions:

If score is greater than 100
    Say \"You win!\"

If score is equal to 0
    Say \"You have no points.\"

If isAlive is true
    Say \"The player is alive.\"

Otherwise
    Say \"The player is defeated.\"

Support:

is equal to
is not equal to
is greater than
is less than
is greater than or equal to
is less than or equal to

==================================================
4. LOOPS
==================================================

Support simple English loops.

Repeat 5 times
    Say \"Hello\"

Repeat until score is 100
    Add 1 to score

Keep doing
    Say \"Running\"

Also support:

For every item in items
    Say item

==================================================
5. FUNCTIONS
==================================================

Functions should also use English.

Example:

Make a function called jump
    Say \"Jumping!\"
    Move player up by 100
    Wait 0.5 seconds
    Move player down by 100

Call it with:

Run jump

Functions should support parameters:

Make a function called greet with name
    Say \"Hello \" + name

Run greet with \"Player\"

Functions should be able to return values:

Make a function called add with a and b
    Return a + b

Let result be the result of add with 5 and 10

==================================================
6. EVENTS
==================================================

Use English event syntax:

When the game starts
    Say \"Game started\"
    Let score be 0

When the player touches the coin
    Add 1 to score
    Delete the coin

When the player touches the hazard
    Reset the player

When the start button is pressed
    Start the game

==================================================
7. MATH
==================================================

Support:

Add 5 to score
Subtract 2 from score
Multiply score by 2
Divide score by 2

Also allow expressions:

Let total be score + coins
Let damage be power * 2
Let average be total / 5

==================================================
8. OBJECTS
==================================================

E# should support objects and game objects.

Example:

Create an object called player

Set player position to 100, 200

Move player right by 50

Move player up by 20

Delete player

Set player speed to 5

Objects should be able to have properties.

==================================================
9. GAME DEVELOPMENT
==================================================

E# should have built-in support for creating games.

Include commands for:

- Players
- Objects
- Sprites
- Images
- Text
- Buttons
- Collision
- Physics
- Movement
- Cameras
- Levels
- Scenes
- Sounds
- Music
- Particles
- Timers
- UI
- Touch input
- Mouse input
- Keyboard input
- Controller input

Example:

Create a player called player

Set player position to 100, 200

When the player touches the coin
    Add 1 to score
    Play sound \"coin\"

==================================================
10. LISTS
==================================================

Support lists using simple English.

Example:

Let items be [\"Sword\", \"Shield\", \"Potion\"]

Add \"Bow\" to items

Remove \"Sword\" from items

Say items

Let firstItem be the first item in items

==================================================
11. CUSTOM COMMANDS
==================================================

Users should be able to create their own commands/functions using English.

Example:

Make a command called give coins with amount
    Add amount to coins

Then:

Give coins with 50

==================================================
12. STRINGS
==================================================

Strings should use quotation marks:

Let name be \"Player\"

Allow combining strings:

Let greeting be \"Hello \" + name

Say greeting

==================================================
13. COMMENTS
==================================================

Use an English-looking comment syntax.

Example:

Note: This gives the player 10 coins

The interpreter should ignore that line.

==================================================
14. ERROR SYSTEM
==================================================

Errors should be written in simple English.

Instead of:

\"SyntaxError: unexpected token\"

Prefer:

\"I don't understand this line. Did you forget to give the variable a value?\"

Give the line number and explain how to fix the problem.

==================================================
15. E# EDITOR
==================================================

Create a complete E# coding editor with:

- Code editor
- Syntax highlighting
- Autocomplete
- Run button
- Stop button
- Console/output
- Error messages
- Line numbers
- Project/file system
- Save/load projects
- Example projects
- Documentation
- Built-in help
- Debugging tools

Autocomplete should suggest E# commands while the user types.

==================================================
16. IMPORTANT LANGUAGE RULE
==================================================

E# must NOT simply be a text converter that changes English-looking commands into another language.

Create an actual E# parser/interpreter/compiler that understands E# syntax.

The language should have its own:

- Syntax rules
- Parser
- Variables
- Data types
- Expressions
- Functions
- Events
- Conditions
- Loops
- Error handling
- Runtime

==================================================
17. DESIGN PHILOSOPHY
==================================================

E# should feel like writing instructions to a computer.

For example, a simple game could look like:

Let score be 0
Let playerName be \"Player\"

When the game starts
    Say \"Welcome \" + playerName

When the player touches the coin
    Add 1 to score
    Say \"Coins: \" + score

If score is greater than 9
    Say \"You win!\"

The syntax should prioritize readability and simplicity over traditional programming conventions.

Build E# so that a complete beginner can look at code and understand roughly what it does without already knowing programming.

LANGUAGE NAME:
E#

TAGLINE:
\"Code in English.\"
"
